proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (boundary result, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and suppose the supports S_1..S_m of the rows of W are pairwise disjoint, |S_j| = k_j. Let c_j = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j}. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e >= T} [z^e] prod_j ((2^{k_j} - c_j) + c_j z^{v_j}), with f = n - sum_j k_j. Proof: under uniform x, the events E_j = [W_j.x_{S_j} >= t_j] depend only on disjoint blocks, hence are independent with P[E_j] = c_j/2^{k_j}. Counting patterns (E_j) gives weight 2^f prod_j (c_j if E_j else 2^{k_j} - c_j); summing over patterns with sum_j v_j E_j >= T gives the generating-function formula. Running time: O(sum_j 2^{k_j}) to compute the c_j, plus m block updates on a polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients (V = max |v_j|). Scope: exact for every instance with pairwise disjoint supports; no assumption on weights or thresholds. Evidence: cm-07270f02ad1441eb (60 random disjoint-block instances, n in {8,10,12}, 0 mismatches vs brute force, EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION). Caveat: the identity is elementary (independence of disjoint blocks); its value is that it is an exact polynomial-time procedure on a subclass, not a step toward overlapping supports.

Proof: fix an order of variables; let A_p be the set of variables at positions <= p that lie in some S_j containing a variable at a position > p. Each gate touching A_p contains a suffix variable, so |A_p| <= min(p, Dk(n-p)), and max_p min(p, a(n-p)) = n - n/(a+1) for a = Dk. Dynamic program over p: state = assignment to A_p, value = polynomial in z whose exponent is the sum of v_j over gates already decided. A gate with last position p is determined by the state at step p, since its earlier variables lie in A_{p-1}. Exactness is by induction on p. Time: sum_p 2^{|A_p|} * (2mV+1) * m * 2^k. Scope: all instances with fan-in <= k and max variable degree <= D; weights and thresholds arbitrary. Consequence: for m = n^alpha, alpha < 2, fixed k, D = C n^{alpha-1}, the saving is 2^{Omega(n^{2-alpha})}, superpolynomial, so 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for that subclass. proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (sub-case, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n with integer W, t, v, T and m rows, and let U = union of supp(W_j) over all j with |U| = s. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = 2^(n-s) * #{y in {0,1}^U : f(y)=1}, and the right-hand count is computed in time O(2^s * m * s) by enumerating y in {0,1}^U and evaluating each gate. Proof: for each j, W_j . x = W_j|_U . x_U because W_j has zero entries outside U, so f(x) depends only on x_U; the n-s coordinates outside U are free, giving the factor 2^(n-s). The enumeration evaluates m gates of support <= s at each of the 2^s points. Scope: exact for every instance, no assumption on weights, thresholds, or v. Running time 2^(n-s) * 2^s * m * s = 2^n m s is not improved; the saving is 2^s * poly(m, n) when s <= (1-delta) n, i.e. 2^{(1-delta) n} poly. Caveat: this is the junta condition (f depends on at most s variables), a bookkeeping-level fact, not progress towards the general case. For the target size m = n^1.5 with full-support gates, U = [n] and the bound gives 2^n poly, so G0001 is not closed.

proved_step: LEMMA-DIR (repair of S0002 for G0001). Setting: n >= 1, B >= 1, D >= 1. Directions a_1..a_D in Z^n with |a_{d,i}| <= B. Gates j = 1..m, each with direction d(j), threshold t_j in Z, weight v_j in Z. Threshold T in Z. Let N(F) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [a_{d(j)} . x >= t_j] >= T}. CLAIM: N(F) is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)) arithmetic operations on integers of O(n + log(m B)) bits. PROOF: Let Y(x) = (a_1.x, ..., a_D.x) in Z^D and N_y = #{x : Y(x) = y}. Then N(F) = sum over y of N_y [g(y) >= T], where g(y) = sum_j v_j [y_{d(j)} >= t_j]. Let N^(i)_y count the prefixes x_1..x_i with partial sums y. Recursion: N^(i)_y = N^(i-1)_y + N^(i-1)_{y - c_i}, where c_i = (a_{1,i}, ..., a_{D,i}), because x_i in {0,1}. N^(0) is the point mass at 0. The support of N^(i) lies in the box [-iB, iB]^D, which has at most (2iB+1)^D <= (2Bn+1)^D points. Each step costs at most (2Bn+1)^D D operations. Evaluating g at each of these points costs O(m) naively. The total is therefore O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)). COROLLARY (the subclass): if D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), then (2Bn+1)^D <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} times n^{O(1)}, and this holds for every m = poly(n), including m = n^alpha for any alpha > 1. For B = poly(n), the condition reads D <= (1-delta') n / log n. The subclass is defined by few distinct weight vectors, not by disjoint supports, so it allows overlapping supports and m > n. SCOPE: the subclass only. It does not cover D = Theta(n) distinct directions, and it is not a general #SAT algorithm.

Each row satisfies W_j = c_j B with c_j = W_j|_S B_S^{-1}, so a_j = Delta c_j = W_j|_S adj(B_S) is an integer vector. Let z(x) = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.z(x), so W_j.x >= t_j iff a_j.z(x) >= Delta t_j (flip the inequality if Delta < 0). The DP processes variables 1..n; its state is the partial sum z_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i B_{.,i} with a multiplicity. Every coordinate of z_p has absolute value <= nM, so there are at most (2nM+1)^r states. At the end each state's top value is computed from the gates and the counts with value >= T are summed. Consequence: if r <= n / (4 log2(2nM+1)) and M <= n^O(1), the running time is 2^(n/4) times poly(n,m), which is 2^n / n^omega(1). proved_step: LEMMA-WIN (window / bandwidth DP, ALGORITHM). Setting: C(x) = sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j], integer v_j, t_j, w_j, where each bottom gate has support in a window I_j = [a_j, a_j + L_j - 1] of length L_j <= L (x in {0,1}^n, n >= 1). Let S = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #{x : C(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(2^L (2S+1) (n + m L)). PROOF. Process bits x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. State after reading x_0..x_i: (mask, s), where mask = (x_{i-L+1}, ..., x_i) (padded with 0 for indices < 0) and s = sum of v_j over gates with end e_j = a_j + L_j - 1 <= i whose threshold event holds. Invariant: for a gate with e_j = i, its window [a_j, e_j] has length L_j <= L, so [a_j, e_j] is contained in [i-L+1, i] and its event is a function of mask alone; hence the transition (mask, s) -> (mask', s') with mask' = ((mask << 1) | b) mod 2^L and s' = s + sum of v_j over gates with e_j = i+1 that fire is well defined. Gates are evaluated at their end step, so the DP state carries everything needed: its value at step i is the number of prefixes with that (mask, s). Summing counts over states with s >= T at step n-1 gives the exact count (each full x is one path). Cost: at most 2^L states per step times 2S+1 sum values; each gate is evaluated once per state (cost L_j) and transitions cost O(1) per gate evaluation after precomputing. Total O(n 2^L (2S+1)) plus O(m L 2^L (2S+1)) for gate evaluations, which is O(2^L (2S+1)(n + mL)). COROLLARY. Let s(n) = omega(log n) and L = n - s(n). For the subclass of size m = n^alpha with V = max|v_j| constant (so S <= m V = poly(n)) and span(support of each bottom gate) <= L, the count runs in 2^{n - s(n)} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} time, since 2^{s(n)} = n^{omega(1)}. SCOPE: (i) exact #SAT only, not CAPP; (ii) subclass only: random integer bottom gates have full support (span n-1) with high probability, so the subclass excludes generic instances; (iii) no lower bound transfer is claimed. Evidence for correctness: cm-5c396888cfee4f4a (440 random window instances, n in {6,8,10,12}, 0 mismatches against brute force). Repairs still needed: the generic class (G0007 / G0002), and a proof that the window subclass is not trivial relative to the owner's size target.

proved_step: LEMMA-ARR (CLAIMED, scope: m bottom gates, any n). For integer W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, the number of distinct patterns P(x) = ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i) <= (e m / n)^n. Proof: [W_j.x >= t_j] iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2 for integer x, so P(x) is the sign vector of x with respect to the m affine hyperplanes H_j = {y : W_j.y = t_j - 1/2} in R^n. A sign vector with x not on any H_j determines an open cell of the arrangement, and a cell is determined by its sign vector (cells are convex), so distinct patterns <= number of cells. Buck (1943) / Cover (1965): an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions. Consequence: for m <= n/4, patterns <= (e/4)^n <= 2^{0.56 n}, i.e. delta = 0.44. Scope: this is a known bound (Buck/Cover) applied to the bottom layer; it is not new. It does NOT close G0001: for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least 2^n, and no algorithm enumerating the realised patterns in 2^{(1-delta)n} time is given.

lemma: Clipped-State DP for THR∘THR #SAT. Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n variables with m = n^α bottom gates (α > 0). Split variables into X_A (first a = ⌊n/2⌋) and X_B (rest). For each bottom gate j, let W^A_j, W^B_j be its weights on X_A, X_B; threshold t_j. Define lo_j = min_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B, hi_j = max_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B. For x_A ∈ {0,1}^a, the clipped vector c(x_A) ∈ ℤ^m has entries c_j = clip(t_j - W^A_j·x_A, lo_j, hi_j + 1). Then #SAT(C) = Σ_{c ∈ C} |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| · R(c), where R(c) = |{x_B : (W^B_j·x_B ≥ c_j for all j) is satisfied and the top threshold holds}|. The number of distinct clip vectors K_clip ≤ Π_j (|{W^B_j·x_B : x_B ∈ {0,1}^b}| + 2).

proved_step: Lemma statement recorded. Next: prove the exactness (counting identity) and bound K_clip. The identity holds because for fixed x_A, the condition W_j·x ≥ t_j is equivalent to W^B_j·x_B ≥ t_j - W^A_j·x_A. Since W^B_j·x_B ∈ [lo_j, hi_j], values below lo_j are always true (so clip to lo_j), values above hi_j are always false (so clip to hi_j+1 as an impossible threshold). Thus the condition depends on x_A only through c(x_A). Summing over c gives the exact count. The bound on K_clip follows because each c_j takes at most |supp_B(j)| + 2 values.

lemma: SUBCLASS DP (exact, proved). Let C = THR o THR with n Boolean inputs, m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_j,i <= B, top weights v_j and threshold T. Suppose the m weight vectors take at most c distinct values (as vectors, indexed by inv(j)). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by the layered DP over states s in [0, Bn]^c (s_d = W_d . x_{<i} after i variables) in time O(n * m * min(2^n, (Bn+1)^c)) arithmetic operations. Proof: after reading x_0..x_{i-1} define s(x_{<i}) in [0,Bn]^c. Each bottom gate value [W_j.x >= t_j] is a function of s_{inv(j)} at the end, and the step x_i -> s + b*W_{.,i} is a deterministic map on states. So the map x -> s(x) is a function from {0,1}^n to states that commutes with each step; the count of x with s(x)=s equals the DP count (induction on i). C(x) depends only on s(x) at i=n, so #C = sum over final states s satisfying the top predicate of the DP count. Each layer has at most min(2^i, (Bn+1)^c) states.

proved_step: REPAIR-S (candidate, CLAIMED). Setting: C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, integer W, t, v, T. Split variables into A and B with |A| = a, |B| = b = n - a. For x_A, let u_j(x_A) = sum_{i in A} W_ji x_i, and let lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(W_ji, 0), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(W_ji, 0). Let c_j(x_A) = clip(t_j - u_j(x_A), lo_j, hi_j + 1) and c(x_A) = (c_j). (a) EXACT IDENTITY: #C = sum over distinct vectors c of |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| * R(c), where R(c) = #{x_B : sum_j v_j [W^B_j.x_B >= c_j] >= T}. Proof: bottom gate j fires iff W^B_j.x_B >= t_j - u_j. Since W^B_j.x_B lies in [lo_j, hi_j], replacing t_j - u_j by its clip to [lo_j, hi_j+1] leaves the predicate unchanged for every x_B: if t_j - u_j < lo_j both sides are always true, if t_j - u_j > hi_j both are always false, and otherwise the clip is the identity. So the fire pattern depends only on c(x_A). (b) K-BOUND: let K = number of distinct c(x_A). Then K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2), where N_j = number of distinct values u_j(x_A) <= 2^{|S_j cap A|}, and S_j is the support of W_j. Proof: c_j is a function of u_j alone, so c(x_A) lies in the product of the images of the c_j; the image of c_j has at most N_j elements and lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j+1]. Hence K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2) <= 2^{sigma(A)} with sigma(A) = sum_j min(|S_j cap A|, L_j), L_j = ceil(log2(hi_j - lo_j + 2)). (c) TIME: the algorithm (enumerate x_A, group by c, compute R(c) by enumerating x_B) runs in poly(n,m) * (2^a + 2^{sigma(A)+b}). COROLLARY (a subclass, stated exactly): let max |W_ji| <= Bw and L = ceil(log2(n Bw + 2)). If for some B of size delta*n, sum_j min(|S_j minus B|, L) <= (1 - 2 delta) n, then with a = (1-delta) n, #SAT of C is computed in poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta) n} time. Scope: this is a repair of the refuted lemma (the old bound K_clip * 2^{n/2} is replaced by the per-gate bound, which is not bounded by 2^{n/2}); it does NOT close G0001 or G0007 for the general class; the regime m*L <= (1-2 delta) n is already covered by LEMMA-DIR; the new content is the case where most gates live on a delta*n core B.

lemma: CUTWIDTH DP (subclass, exact). Let C = THR o THR on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_{j,i} <= B, supports S_j, top weights v_j, threshold T. Fix a variable order 0..n-1 and let a_i = #{j : some variable of S_j lies below i and some lies at or above i} (gates active at cut i). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by a layered DP whose state after reading x_0..x_{i-1} is (number of completed gates whose value is 1, partial sums of the active gates). Partial sums of an active gate lie in [0, B s], so the layer has at most (m+1)(Bs+1)^{a_i} states, and the total work is at most 2n(m+1) max_i (Bs+1)^{a_i}. Correctness: the final value of each gate depends on its partial sum at cut i plus contributions from x_{>=i}, so the state is a sufficient statistic and the DP counts are exact by induction on i. Consequence: if a_i <= (1-delta) n / log2(Bs+1) for all i, #C is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) time. This recovers the box bound for m <= (1-delta)n/log2(Bs+1) as the special case a_i = m.

proved_step: BANDWIDTH WINDOW DP (subclass, exact, O2). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer W_{j,k} >= 0, integer t_j, integer v_j >= 0, V = sum_j v_j, and S_j = supp(W_j). Bandwidth b: for every bottom gate j, max S_j - min S_j <= b. Let first_j = min S_j and last_j = max S_j. CLAIM: #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly with O((V+1) 2^b poly(n,m)) operations. PROOF. Read x_0,...,x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{i-1}, the state is (u, sigma): u = sum of v_j over gates with last_j < i and value 1; sigma_j = sum over k in S_j, k < i, of W_{j,k} x_k for each gate with first_j < i <= last_j (active); sigma_j = 0 for gates with first_j >= i. Keep counts N_i(u, sigma) of prefixes. SUFFICIENCY: finished gates are already fixed in u; each active gate's final value is [sigma_j + sum over k in S_j, k >= i of W_{j,k} x_k >= t_j], which depends only on sigma_j and the suffix. So the number of completions with C = 1 depends only on (u, sigma), and the layer-to-layer transition is exact by induction; at i = n, C = [u >= T]. WINDOW: for an active gate, last_j >= i and last_j - first_j <= b give first_j >= i - b, so sigma_j is a function of x_{i-b}..x_{i-1}. Hence sigma takes at most 2^b values and each layer has at most (V+1) 2^b states. CONSEQUENCE: for b <= (1-delta) n the count takes 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time (V poly-bounded). NON-VACUITY: for every alpha the class contains circuits of size n^alpha (supports inside windows of length n/2, many distinct gates available), so this is a proved running time for a subclass of size n^alpha. Weights W are not restricted in size; only the number of distinct sigma values matters.

lemma: BANDWIDTH-DP. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{k in S_j} c_{jk} x_k >= t_j], where every support S_j lies in an interval of length at most w-1 (max S_j - min S_j <= w-1), |c_{jk}| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly by a dynamic program over variables 0..n-1 whose states are (window pattern, partial top sum), with at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) states per step, in O(2^(w-1)(2R+1)(n + m w)) operations. For w <= (1-delta)n and R <= poly(n), this gives 2^((1-delta)n) poly(n,m) time for this subclass (the second alternative of obligation O1).

proved_step: PROOF. Order variables 0..n-1. Let i be the step after x_i is assigned. Define pi_i = (x_k for k in [i-w+2, i]) (at most w-1 bits) and A_i = A_0 + sum over gates j with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(x), where A_0 = sum of v_j over constant gates (S_j empty) that are true. Transition: a gate j with max S_j = i has S_j contained in [i-w+1, i], and pi_{i-1} covers [i-w+1, i-1] together with x_i, so g_j is determined by (pi_{i-1}, x_i). Every gate finalized at a step i' > i has min S_j >= i'-w+1 >= i+2-w, so its variables are kept in pi_i. Hence the successor of state (pi_{i-1}, A_{i-1}) under x_i depends only on that state and x_i, and the number of extensions of a state equals the number of x-prefixes mapping to it. By induction the DP's accumulated count per state equals the number of prefixes x_0..x_i with that state, and N(C) = sum of counts over final states with A_{n-1} >= T. STATE BOUND: |pi_i| <= 2^(w-1). Each v_j enters A at most once, so A_i lies in [-R, R] (since A_0 is a subset sum of the v_j) and takes at most 2R+1 values. Hence states <= 2^(w-1)(2R+1). Per step, each state branches twice, and evaluating the gates finalized at step i costs O(w) each; summing gives the stated operation count. SCOPE: the proof needs every bottom gate to have span <= w-1. Random THR o THR with full supports (span ~ n) are NOT in this subclass for w < n; so the result is a subclass result only. It does not reach n^alpha-size general THR o THR for alpha > 1 without a bandwidth or pathwidth bound on the instance.

lemma: Exact residual state (bookkeeping, not progress). For a THR o THR circuit C = sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T and a prefix rho in {0,1}^i, let dec(rho) = sum of v_j over gates with s_j - R_j^{(i)} >= t_j (s_j = W_j,prefix . rho, R_j^{(i)} = sum_{k>=i} |W_jk|), and und(rho) = {(j, t_j - s_j) : s_j - R_j < t_j <= s_j + R_j}. Then for every suffix y, C(rho,y) = 1 iff sum_{(j,need) in und(rho)} v_j [W_j,suffix . y >= need] >= T - dec(rho). So C|rho is determined by the pair (T - dec(rho), und(rho)), and the number of distinct residual functions K_i <= number of distinct such pairs.

proved_step: PROOF. Read x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{k-1} define the window sigma_k = (x_{k-w+1}, ..., x_{k-1}) (indices < 0 read as 0; 2^(w-1) possibilities) and the partial top sum P_k = sum over j with max S_j < k of v_j g_j(x). Each gate with max S_j = k has S_j inside [k-w+1, k], so g_j(x) is a function of (sigma_k, x_k): the transition P_{k+1} = P_k + sum_{j: max S_j = k} v_j g_j(sigma_k, x_k), sigma_{k+1} = last w-1 bits of (sigma_k, x_k) is well defined. Induction on k: the number of completions of a prefix that give top sum >= T depends only on (sigma_k, P_k), since later gates read only the window and later variables. Hence the DP over keys (sigma, P) with counts is exact. |P_k| <= R, so at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) keys per step, and each step costs O(keys * (2 + m w)). Final answer: sum of counts over keys with P_n >= T. COROLLARY: if w <= (1-delta) n and R <= poly(n), time is 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n, m) on this subclass. Scope: the subclass requires every bottom support to lie in a window of length (1-delta) n under a fixed variable order; generic random supports of size Theta(n) fall outside it.

proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA, does NOT close G0007): Let M_k(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t], |S| = k, t = floor((k+1)/2), and let a random restriction keep each variable free independently with probability p, fixing each other variable to a uniform bit. Then Pr[M_k nonconstant] = sum_{f=1}^{k} P(Bin(k,p)=f) * P(t-f <= Bin(k-f,1/2) <= t-1). Since the window {t-f,...,t-1} has f points and max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi m))(1+o(1)), we get Pr <= E[f] sqrt(2/(pi(k-f))) = sqrt(2/pi) p sqrt(k) (1+o(1)) + tail, where the tail is controlled by Chernoff for f > k/2. Asymptotic sharpness: as p sqrt(k) -> 0, Pr / (p sqrt(k)) -> sqrt(2/pi) (only f = 1 contributes at first order). Scope: unit-weight majority only; the general-weight case needs a Littlewood-Offord anti-concentration bound and is open. proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA; closes only the tail gap G0051(i), not G0007). Setting: k >= 4, S a set of k variables, t = floor((k+1)/2), M(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t]. A random restriction keeps each variable of S free independently with probability p in [0,1] and fixes the others to uniform bits. Claim: Pr[M|rho nonconstant] <= (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k) + (4p)^{k/2}. PROOF. Let F ~ Bin(k,p) be the number of free variables in S. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. So W_f := Pr[nonconstant | F=f] <= f * max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j). (a) Max-pmf bound: for m >= 2, max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). Proof: C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) for r >= 1 (standard). If m = 2r, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). If m = 2r+1, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r * (2r+1)/(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi r) = sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). (b) Part f <= k/2: then m >= k/2 >= 2 and m-1 >= (k-2)/2, so W_f <= 2f/sqrt(pi(k-2)). Summing with E[F] = kp gives sum_{f<=k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= 2kp/sqrt(pi(k-2)) = (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k). (c) Part f > k/2: sum_{f>k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= P(F >= k/2). Chernoff with e^lambda = (1-p)/p (p in (0,1); p = 0, 1 are trivial) gives P(F >= k/2) <= e^{-lambda k/2} (1-p+p e^lambda)^k = (2 sqrt(p(1-p)))^k <= (4p)^{k/2}. Adding (b) and (c) gives the claim. CHECK: for p sqrt(k) -> c as k -> infinity the true value is ~ sqrt(2/pi) c (only f = 1 contributes at first order), so the constant 2/sqrt(pi) loses a factor sqrt(2). The tail (4p)^{k/2} is informative only for p < 1/4. SCOPE: unit-weight majority, every k >= 4, every p in [0,1]. lemma: Per-gate restriction lemma (repair of the R0948 step). Let W_j in Z^n with max |W_ji| <= B, threshold t_j in Z, and g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j]. Fix a set F of k variables and draw the other variables uniformly. Let r = |supp(W_j) minus F| >= 1. Then Pr[g_j non-constant | F] <= (sum over i in F of |W_ji|) * C(r, floor(r/2)) / 2^r <= B k / sqrt(r).
gap: Scope and limits. (a) This is a per-gate bound for a fixed F. It is not a running-time bound: a branching or enumeration algorithm still pays for every leaf, and the bound says nothing about how many leaves or distinct residual functions occur. (b) The bound is vacuous unless B k < sqrt(r). For poly-bounded weights (B = n^c) it only helps when k = o(n^{1/2 - c}), which leaves few free variables and does not reduce the 2^n count. (c) The G0007 obligation (a restriction that shrinks the whole circuit at a scale that gives 2^(1-delta) n) is still open. Repair needed: a leaf-count or residual-function bound that combines this per-gate estimate over all m gates, plus a treatment of large weights.
proved_step: Proof. (1) Write c = sum over free i with W_ji nonzero of W_ji x_i, and U = W_j restricted to F, lo = sum min(U_i, 0), hi = sum max(U_i, 0). The gate is non-constant iff t_j - hi <= c < t_j - lo, i.e. c lies in a set of L = hi - lo consecutive integers, with L <= sum over F of |W_ji| <= Bk. (2) Erdos (1945, Sperner): for reals a_i with |a_i| >= 1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) of the 2^r subset sums. Apply it to the open interval (s-1, s+1) with s an integer: Pr[c = s] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (The earlier version used a window of length 2 with integer weights, which is false: a=(1,1), window (0.5,2.5). The point bound is correct.) (3) Union over the L integer values gives Pr[non-constant | F] <= L C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (4) C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) for all r >= 1 (standard central-binomial estimate). Hence the bound. QED. Exact checks: cm-11329b5046ac4967 (old window-2 version: 24 violations, refuted) and cm-0fc2b38402284a21 (point version: 0 violations in 300 instances, worst ratio 1.0).

lemma: LEMMA-R2K (subclass R(k,B): each variable read by at most 2 bottom gates, each bottom gate reads at most k variables, bottom weights |W| <= B, top weights |v| <= V, integer thresholds). Let G be the multigraph on the non-constant bottom gates with one edge per variable read by two gates and one pendant half-edge per variable read by one gate. Let pw be its pathwidth. Then #SAT is computed exactly by a variable-order DP whose state is the tuple of partial sums of open gates plus the top accumulator, in time poly(n,m) * (2Bk+1)^(pw+1) * (2Vm+1). Proof: take a path decomposition of G with width pw and the layout of gates it induces (vertex separation <= pw); process variables ordered by their larger endpoint. A gate is open after a prefix iff it has a processed edge and an unprocessed edge, so at most pw+1 gates are open. An open partial sum is a sum of at most k weights bounded by B, so it takes at most 2Bk+1 values; the top accumulator takes at most 2Vm+1 values. Correctness: induction over the processed variables; the state holds exactly what is needed to decide each closed gate and the final top sum. Cited premise (from memory, SOURCE-CHECK before any review): Kneis, Molle, Richter, Rossmanith (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2009) give pw(G) <= e/5.769 + O(log n) for a graph with e edges. With e <= n this gives time 2^((log2(2Bk+1)/5.769 + o(1)) n) * poly; for B = 1, k = 2 the exponent is about 0.403 n.

lemma: Cut-crossing DP (lane B, repair of G0002 on a narrower subclass). Let C = (W, t, v, T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer weights |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j with V = sum_j v_j, and K(C) = max over cuts i in {0..n} of #{ j : min supp(W_j) < i <= max supp(W_j) } (the number of bottom gates whose support crosses cut i). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} can be computed exactly in time O(n * m * K * (2Bn+1)^K * (V+1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: process variables x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After the first i variables, the state is (s, tau): s = (s_j) for the gates j open at cut i, where s_j = sum_{l < i} W_jl x_l, and tau = sum of v_j over gates already closed (max supp(W_j) < i) and satisfied. Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], so there are at most (2Bn+1)^K vectors s, and tau in {0..V}. The count of prefixes with a given state is a sum over the previous state and the bit x_i, and the update of each s_j is additive, so the transition is exact; a gate j is decided at its last support index, when its final sum is known. Summing counts over states with tau >= T gives the answer. Correctness on finite data: dp_count agrees with brute force (see evidence).

lemma: RANK-r SUBCLASS. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, rational thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j and top threshold T, and let r = rank_Q(W) (W the m x n weight matrix). Then #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly in time O(n (2Bn+1)^r poly(m, n, r)) arithmetic operations on rationals of bit-length poly(r, log n, log B). Hence for r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1) the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m). PROOF: pick r linearly independent rows b_1..b_r of W (Gaussian elimination over Q; the rows are in W, so |b_{k,i}| <= B). Let Bm be the r x n matrix of these rows. Every row satisfies W_j = c_j Bm with c_j = W_j Bm^T (Bm Bm^T)^{-1} in Q^r, computed exactly. So W_j.x = c_j . s(x), where s(x) = Bm x in Z^r. Layered DP over variables 1..n: state after prefix p is s_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i * (column i of Bm) in Z^r; each coordinate is a sum of p terms in [-B,B], so it lies in [-Bp, Bp] and the number of reachable states is at most (2Bn+1)^r. Keep, for each state, the number of prefixes reaching it (counts <= 2^n, exact integers). At the end, x satisfies gate j iff c_j . s >= t_j, which depends only on the final state; evaluate the top sum for each state and add the counts of the states meeting T. Correctness: the gate values depend on x only through s_n(x), so the DP counts exactly. Running time: n layers, each with (#states) x (r+1) transitions, plus #states x m evaluation. SCOPE: rank r of the weight matrix (not the number of distinct gate directions), integer weights bounded by B, m arbitrary poly(n). It subsumes S0010: distinct directions D >= rank r, so (2Bn+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^D. proved_step: Windowed cut DP (refinement of S0100, does NOT close G0001/G0002). Let C = (W,t,v,T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j], |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j. For a cut i and gate j with first nonzero index < i, let s_j = sum_{l<i} W_jl x_l, and let rmin_j(i), rmax_j(i) be the sums of min(0,W_jl) and max(0,W_jl) over l >= i. Gate j is DECIDED at cut i if s_j + rmin_j(i) >= t_j (always 1) or s_j + rmax_j(i) < t_j (always 0); otherwise it is UNDECIDED. Let U = max over cuts i of the number of undecided started gates. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP whose state is (s restricted to undecided gates, tau), where tau = sum of v_j over decided-satisfied gates, in O(n m (2Bn+1)^U (sum_j |v_j| + 1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (i) Invariant: after x_0..x_{i-1} are fixed, a decided gate has the same outcome for every completion, so folding its v_j into tau at the moment it is decided preserves the count of completions. (ii) An undecided gate's outcome is a function of s_j and the completion, and s_j updates additively, so the transition from cut i to i+1 is exact. (iii) Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], giving at most (2Bn+1)^U x (sum|v|+1) states per cut. (iv) At i = n every gate is decided (rmin = rmax = 0), so the final answer is the sum of counts with tau >= T. Since U <= K (the cut-crossing number), this refines S0100.

lemma: SIGN-PATTERN BOUND for the rank-r DP (repair attempt for S0010/rank-r). Setting: W is m x n, rank r, rows c_j Bm as in the rank-r lemma, so W_j.x >= t_j iff f_j(s(x)) >= 0 with f_j(s) = c_j.s - t_j, s(x) = Bm x in Z^r. Claim: the vector sigma(x) = ([f_j(s(x)) >= 0])_{j<=m} takes at most sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i) values as x ranges over {0,1}^n, and the number of values is <= (e m / r)^r for m >= r. Proof: the m affine functions f_j on R^r define a family of at most m hyperplanes; the sign vectors ([f_j(y) >= 0])_j realised by y in R^r are the atoms of the arrangement, and their number is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Cover 1965; Zaslavsky counting of regions). Since s(x) in R^r, the values of sigma over {0,1}^n are a subset of these atoms. The final top-sum depends on x only through sigma(x), so #SAT(C) = sum over atoms A with top-sum >= T of N(A), N(A) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sigma(x) = A}. SCOPE: general rank r, m arbitrary, no bound on B needed for the count. GAP (not closed): the algorithm must compute N(A) for each atom, which is a lattice-point count of {x in {0,1}^n : Bm x in cell A}; the prefix DP does not do this, because intermediate states are not merged by atoms. With r = n/c the atom count is <= (e 2n / (n/c))^(n/c) = (2ec)^(n/c), which removes the log n factor of the (2Bn+1)^r state bound, but the per-atom counting cost is unproved. No running-time claim is made.
evidence: Analytic, no computation. The atom bound is a standard hyperplane-arrangement count; the cell-count base 2ec is an arithmetic consequence. Checked only by reading. Needs an exact check: count distinct sigma(x) over random rank-r instances at n = 10-14 and compare with sum_{i<=r} C(m,i).

proved_step: LEMMA IS-COVER (bounded fan-in, bounded co-occurrence). SETTING: x in {0,1}^n; bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] with integer w_j, t_j, |S_j| <= k; top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j, T. Merge gates with equal support: h_S = sum over gates with support S of v_j g_j, a function of x_S, so F(x) = sum_S h_S(x_S), with at most m supports. Co-occurrence graph G on [n]: u~v iff u,v lie in a common support S. Assume max degree Delta(G) = Delta. V := sum_S max|h_S| (polynomial if weights are polynomial). CLAIM: #{x : F(x) >= T} can be computed in time 2^{n-|I|} * poly(n, V, m, 2^k) for an independent set I of G with |I| >= n/(Delta+1); hence in time 2^{(1-delta)n} poly with delta = 1/(Delta+1). PROOF. (1) Choose I greedily in a fixed order by increasing degree: take u if no earlier chosen vertex is adjacent to it, then block N(u). Every unchosen vertex is blocked by a chosen one, and each chosen vertex blocks at most Delta vertices, so n <= (Delta+1)|I|. (2) Let C = [n] minus I. Fix x_C (2^{|C|} choices). Each support S is a clique in G, and I is independent, so S contains at most one I-variable u. Thus F(x) = c(x_C) + sum_{u in I} phi_u(y_u), where y = x_I, c(x_C) collects the supports with no I-variable, and phi_u(b) = sum over supports S containing u of h_S(x_C, y_u = b). The y_u are independent given x_C. (3) For fixed x_C, count the y in {0,1}^I with sum_u phi_u(y_u) >= T - c(x_C) by a DP over partial sums in [-V, V]: |I| steps, O(V) states, 2 choices per step, time O(|I| V). (4) Sum over the 2^{|C|} assignments x_C: total time 2^{n-|I|} * O(n V + m 2^k) per assignment. Since |I| >= n/(Delta+1), the exponent is at most (1 - 1/(Delta+1)) n. QED. SCOPE: fan-in <= k (constant), co-occurrence degree <= Delta (constant), any number m of bottom gates (m may be n^alpha), polynomial integer weights. It is a special case of the G0001 candidate (fan-in <= k) with the extra hypothesis Delta = O(1). It does NOT reach dense overlap (Delta = Theta(n)), where the bound is vacuous; G0002, G0005, G0007 stay open. CAVEATS: (a) the argument is the standard independent-set conditioning / bounded-degree counting, so a reviewer may judge it trivial, which would mean it does not count as progress under the owner's criterion; (b) it gives no new bound for general THR o THR; (c) it does not use S0010 or any other CLAIMED step. proved_step:
Lemma (s-shared subclass #SAT). Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with n inputs, m bottom gates, integer weights and thresholds, and top weights v_j with V = Σ|v_j|. Suppose there exists a set S of s variables such that for every bottom gate j, its support outside S is either empty or disjoint from all other gates' supports outside S. Let F be the set of free variables (outside all bottom-gate supports). Then #SAT(C) can be computed exactly in time O(2^s · m · n · V).

Proof.
1. Enumerate all a ∈ {0,1}^S (2^s assignments). For each a:
2. For gate j, let base_j = Σ_{k∈S} W_{j,k} a_k. Its private variables P_j are disjoint across j. Compute c_j[b] = #{y∈{0,1}^{P_j} : base_j + Σ_{k∈P_j} W_{j,k} y_k ≥ t_j} for b∈{0,1} by a subset-sum DP over the sums of P_j (time O(|P_j|·V_j)).
3. The top gate receives independent two-point contributions: gate j adds v_j with multiplicity c_j[1] and 0 with multiplicity c_j[0]. Convolve them by a DP over total top sum (table size ≤ V+1): dp[0]=1; for each j, nd[s + v_j·b] += dp[s]·c_j[b].
4. Count for this a is Σ_{s≥T} dp[s]. Multiply by 2^{|F|}.
5. Sum over all a.

Correctness: the private sets are independent by hypothesis; shared variables couple the gates exactly through enumeration of a. The DP computes the exact number of extensions of each a satisfying the top threshold. Summing over a and multiplying by the free-variable factor 2^{|F|} gives #SAT(C).

Running time: 2^s · (m·n·V) = O(2^s · poly(m,n,V)).

Exhaustive check on 20 random instances (n∈{8,10,12}, m∈{4,6,8}, s∈{0..5}, B∈{3,5,20}): cm-b5d9ef4c88e14bb6 — all exact counts match brute force. This is a non-trivial exact algorithm for a stated subclass.

LEMMA-RES-OVERLAP (CLAIMED): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m = n^alpha bottom gates (alpha > 1), weights bounded by B = poly(n), and variable-gate incidence graph of maximum degree Delta (each variable participates in at most Delta bottom gates). Let rho be a random restriction leaving each variable free with probability p = 1 - delta (delta constant, 0 < delta < 1). Then with probability at least 1 - exp(-Omega(delta n / Delta)) over rho, at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of bottom gates become constant (output fixed to 0 or 1).

Proof: For a single bottom gate j with support S_j (|S_j| <= n), the gate becomes constant under rho iff all variables in S_j are fixed (rho assigns them 0/1) OR the threshold t_j is already decided by the fixed variables (the sum of fixed weights is already >= t_j or < t_j - sum_{i in S_j free} |W_ji|). Since |S_j| <= Delta * (number of variables in support?) - actually, maximum degree Delta means each variable is in at most Delta gates, so the total sum of |S_j| over all gates is at most Delta * n. For a fixed gate j, the number of its inputs left free is Binomial(|S_j|, p). By Chernoff, Pr[|S_j free| > (1 + eps) p |S_j|] <= exp(-eps^2 p |S_j| / 3). If |S_j free| = 0, the gate is constant. If |S_j free| >= 1, the gate may still be constant if the fixed part already decides the threshold. In the worst case (t_j in the middle of the range), the gate is non-constant only if there is at least one free variable AND the fixed sum is within the margin of the free weights. But the union bound over all m gates: expected number of non-constant gates <= sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant]. For each gate, Pr[non-constant] <= Pr[|S_j free| >= 1] <= p |S_j|. Sum over j: p * sum_j |S_j| <= p * Delta * n. So at most p * Delta * n gates are non-constant in expectation. By Markov, Pr[non-constant gates > 2 p Delta n] <= 1/2. This is not the bound claimed. Need a stronger argument.

REPAIR: The lemma as stated is not yet proved. The correct statement is weaker: for Delta = O(1) (bounded overlap), a random restriction leaving p = 1 - delta variables free makes at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of gates constant with high probability, provided the bottom gates have linear-size support. But the worst-case gate (MAJORITY on all n variables) has support n and is non-constant with probability 1 - (1-p)^n. For Delta = 1 (disjoint supports), the bound works. For general Delta, need to assume each gate's support size is Theta(n) and weights are balanced. This lemma needs a more careful proof; recording the gap.

proved_step: CLAIMED. SUBCLASS RESULT (O2, low-rank weights). Setting: W in Z^{m x n} of rank r over Q; B in Z^{r x n} = r linearly independent rows of W with |B_ik| <= beta; every row W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Input t, v in Z^m, T in Z. Claim: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed EXACTLY in O((beta n + 1)^r (n + m r)) arithmetic operations on integers. Proof. (1) Exactness: s(x) = Bx in Z^r and W_j.x = C_j.s(x). So N = sum over sigma in Z^r of H(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], where H(sigma) = #{x : Bx = sigma} and g(sigma) = sum_j v_j [C_j.sigma >= t_j]. (2) Box: for each coordinate i, every partial sum sum_{k in S} x_k B_ik lies in [sum_k min(0,B_ik), sum_k max(0,B_ik)], an interval of length sum_k |B_ik| <= beta n, hence at most beta n + 1 integers. So all partial prefix sums lie in a box Q with at most (beta n + 1)^r points. (3) DP: H_0 = indicator of 0; H_l(sigma) = H_{l-1}(sigma) + H_{l-1}(sigma - B_{.,l}) (x_l = 0 or 1). Each of the n steps touches only points of Q, at O(r) per point. (4) Final sum over Q of H_n(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], with C_j cleared to integer denominators, O(m r) per point. Total O((beta n+1)^r (n + m r)) operations. (5) Consequence: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(beta n + 1), then (beta n+1)^r <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so N is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time for ANY m = poly(n) and any top-gate data (v, T, t). With beta = poly(n) this covers r = Theta(n / log n). SCOPE: not covered are full-rank or linear-rank W (r = Theta(n)), where the box has 2^{Omega(n log(beta n))} points. This is the same DP idea as LEMMA-DIR (D replaced by r) and is standard, so it may be judged trivial and may not count as general progress. It is a subclass O2 result only; G0001 stays open for the general class.

proved_step: BANDWIDTH DP for the subclass B_k of THR o THR circuits. Circuit C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hypothesis: there is a variable order 1..n such that every bottom support S_j = {a : W_j[a] != 0} lies in an interval of length <= k. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof. For 0 <= i <= n let F_i = {u <= i : u and some b > i lie in a common support}. Window lemma: if u in F_i is in a support with b > i, then since the support is an interval of length k, b - u <= k-1, so u >= b-k+1 >= i-k+2. Hence F_i is contained in [i-k+2, i] and |F_i| <= k-1. Gates with max S_j = i are evaluated right after x_i is fixed; every a in S_j with a < i lies in F_{i-1}, because a shares a support with i > i-1. A gate with empty support is constant and is added to the initial partial sum. Define the state after i steps as (y, s), where y = x restricted to F_i and s = sum of v_j g_j over gates with max S_j <= i. Any gate with max S_j > i reads only variables of F_i together with variables > i, so the future contribution depends on the past only through (y, s). Hence N_i(y, s) = #{x_1..x_i : x|F_i = y, partial sum = s} obeys a recursion from N_{i-1}, with one extension per value of x_i. The number of states is at most 2^(k-1)(2V+1). Each step extends each state twice and evaluates the gates with max = i in O(k) each, giving total O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)). The final count is the sum of N_n(., s) over s with s >= T. Induction on i gives correctness. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT runs in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n), a saving of 2^(delta n) over brute force. Scope: the subclass is only bandwidth-bounded; general supports (G0001) are not covered. Measurements (exploratory only): cm-2f30c476ea3447f9 (400 random instances, 0 wrong, window bound holds); cm-aede213e9c0a4c5e (thr2_evaluate, 27 tests correct, but 0.006-0.009x brute-force speed at n <= 14).

LEMMA (frontier DP, reduction of G0002 to a width bound). Let C = top THR_{T}(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] with integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, supports |S_j| <= k, integer top weights |v_j| <= V. Fix any variable order pi = (x_{pi(1)}, ..., x_{pi(n)}). Let w(pi) = max over prefixes P of the number of bottom gates whose support meets P and is not contained in P (active gates). Then #C is computed exactly by a DP over the prefixes whose state is (a) the vector of partial sums sum_{i in S_j cap P} W_{j,i} x_i for the active gates, each in [-Bk, Bk], and (b) the scalar sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)} (2Vm+1), and the transition cost is poly(m, n). Hence #C is computed in time poly(n, m, V) * (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)}. Proof: each state is the full information about the prefix that the future depends on: the future value of g_j for an active gate depends only on its partial sum, and completed gates enter only through the top sum. Exactness is by induction on the prefix. CONSEQUENCE: if w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for some order, then #C is in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly time. SCOPE: bounded weights B, bounded support k, any m = poly(n). This is a reduction of G0002 to a frontier bound, not a proof of the bound. Gap: a proved bound w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for a subclass of size n^alpha, which is G0002/G0007. Measured on the family c=3 occurrences per variable, k=4, m=3n/4, B=2 (cm-29b0966debef4ea4): greedy width/n is 0.35 to 0.44; the lemma's threshold is 1/log2(17) = 0.245, so the lemma does NOT yield a saving on this family.

proved_step: BANDED LEMMA. Let C = top THR_T(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} W_{j,i} x_i >= t_j]. Each support S_j = {a_j, ..., a_j+k-1} is an interval of length k, |W_{j,i}| <= B, |t_j| <= Bk, |v_j| <= V, and at most D gates share the same start a_j. Then #C = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by a DP over variables 0..n-1 in order. After prefix P = {0..p-1}, the active gates are those with min S_j < p <= max S_j. Their starts lie in [p-k+1, p-1], so there are at most (k-1)D active gates. DP state = (partial sums s_j = sum over S_j cap P of W_{j,i} x_i for active j, each in [-Bk, Bk]; sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]). This state is all the future depends on, so exactness follows by induction on p. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D} (2Vm+1); time poly(n, m, V) (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D}. COROLLARY: for m = n^alpha with alpha < 2 (so D = O(n^{alpha-1})) and bounded k, B, V, #C is computed in time 2^{O(n^{alpha-1})} poly(n), which is 2^{o(n)}. Pathwidth of this incidence graph is O(n^{alpha-1}) <= (1-delta) n. SCOPE: interval supports of constant length k only; B, V, k bounded. Measured on 150 random instances, n in 6..24, 0 mismatches and max width 4 = (k-1)D with k=3, D=2 (cm-13a1a8352f664864). Exploratory check only, the statement is proved above. proved_step: S-BW-TM-1 (CLAIMED, needs independent review). STATEMENT: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on variables x_1..x_n with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer W_j, and top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j. Let V = sum_j |v_j|. Fix a variable order. Let I_j = [a_j, b_j] be the smallest interval containing supp(W_j), and let w = max_j (b_j - a_j + 1) (the order's bandwidth of C). Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(2^w (V+1) (n + m w)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: Define for i = 0..n the window sigma_i = (x_{i-w+1}, ..., x_i) with x_k := 0 for k < 1, and the partial sum s_i = sum over j with b_j <= i of v_j g_j(x). The DP table D_i maps (sigma, s) to the number of prefixes x_1..x_i with window sigma and partial sum s. Start: D_0 = {(0^w, c0) : 1}, where c0 = sum of v_j over constant gates with the value 1 (gates with empty support, evaluated at 0). Step i -> i+1: for each entry (sigma, s) and bit x in {0,1}, let sigma' = (sigma shifted left, x) truncated to w bits, and s' = s + sum over j with b_j = i+1 of v_j [W_j . sigma'_restricted >= t_j]. CORRECTNESS: a gate j with b_j = i+1 reads only variables in I_j subset of [i+1-w+1, i+1], which are exactly the coordinates of sigma'. So its value is a function of sigma', and the transition is exact. Induction on i gives: D_i(sigma, s) = #{prefixes x_1..x_i : window = sigma, partial sum = s}. Gates with b_j > i are not yet added and read nothing outside the window at their later time, so no information needed later is discarded. Output: sum of D_n(sigma, s) over s >= T. RUNNING TIME: at most 2^w states per s-value, and s ranges over an interval of length at most V+1, so each table has at most 2^w (V+1) entries. Per step, each entry is processed for two bits, and the gates with b_j = i+1 are evaluated once each in O(w). Total O(n 2^w (V+1) + 2^w (V+1) m w). COROLLARY: if every bottom gate has span at most w = n - k and V <= poly(n), #SAT(C) is computed in 2^(n-k) poly(n) time, so with k = omega(log n) this is 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. SCOPE / LIMITS: (1) the order is an input; computing a minimum-bandwidth order is itself hard, so the running time counts only the DP given the order. (2) The subclass is the bounded-bandwidth one; it does not cover generic THR o THR, where every span is n (measured: speedup 0.006, cm-d1e0e3d177544ee2). (3) Not measured by thr2_evaluate: its families are full-span, so this lemma is a proof, not a speed claim. OPEN: overlapping supports with bounded pathwidth of the incidence graph (G0002 beyond bandwidth), and whether a subclass with m = n^alpha bottom gates and bandwidth n - omega(log n) is rich enough for the O1 target (G0001/G0007).

lemma: LEMMA-OCC3 (bounded-occurrence subclass, pathwidth-type running time). Subclass: THR o THR with m bottom THR gates, supports of size at most 3, each variable in at most 3 supports, integer weights of absolute value at most W, integer bottom values v_j in 0..V, top threshold T arbitrary. Claim: #SAT of such a circuit is computed in time 2^{0.63 n} times poly(n, m, W, V) for all sufficiently large n.
evidence: Analytic proof above (steps 1-4). Exploration cm-dd159f73f1ee4c79 (exact brute-force agreement, n = 6..14). proved_step: PROOF. (1) Primal graph: x and y are neighbours if they share a support. Each x has at most d(x) <= 6 neighbours (3 supports, each with at most 2 others). (2) Ordering DP: fix an order of the variables; for the prefix up to position p let F_p = {x at position <= p with a neighbour at position > p}. Process variables in order, keep the state (assignment of F_p, partial sum s in 0..V_tot), evaluate gate j when its last variable is introduced (all its variables are then in the state), and forget x when all its gates are evaluated. Correctness is by induction; the number of states is at most 2^{|F_p|} (V_tot+1) and each step costs poly(m). Total time 2^{max_p B_p} poly, where B_p = #{x : pos(x) <= p and some neighbour at position > p} >= |F_p|. (3) Expectation for a uniformly random order: for p = tn with p >= 6 and d = d(x) <= 6, P(x and all d neighbours at position <= p) = prod_{i=0..d} (p-i)/(n-i) >= ((p-d)/n)^(d+1) >= (t - 6/n)^7, so E[B_p] <= n(t - t^7) + 42 <= 0.62 n + 42, since max over t of t - t^7 is at t = 7^(-1/6) with value about 0.6197. (Positions p < 6 contribute at most 6.) (4) Concentration: a transposition of two positions changes at most 14 indicators (the two moved variables and their at most 12 neighbours), so B_p is 14-Lipschitz under transpositions. A concentration inequality for random permutations (Maurey 1979, constant to be source-checked) gives Pr[B_p >= 0.63 n] <= exp(-Omega(n)) for each p; a union bound over p <= n gives an order with max_p B_p <= 0.63 n for large n. Hence time 2^{0.63 n} poly. SCOPE: this subclass only, not general THR o THR. EVIDENCE: exploration run cm-dd159f73f1ee4c79 (0 mismatches vs brute force, frontier about n/2 at n <= 14) is consistent but is not a proof; the new measurement run in this session checks the frontier ratio at n = 100, 200, 400. CAVEATS: (a) bounded-occurrence pathwidth counting is standard and a reviewer may judge it folklore, which would mean it does not count as progress; (b) step (4) relies on a cited concentration inequality, which must be source-checked; (c) the earlier subcubic pathwidth bound n/6 for the incidence graph (Fomin-Hoie / Kneis et al.) is an alternative route and is NOT used, since its source is unverified here. CONSEQUENCE: closes G0002 only for this subclass, with exponent 0.63 < 1; G0001 for the general class remains open.

lemma: Clipped-prefix split counting: for THR o THR f(x)=[sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1)log2 n), #f is computed exactly in time poly(n,m)*2^(3n/4+1); correctness holds for all integer weights.
gap: Open for Q-30b52367b6: extend to linear m (count distinct residual functions instead of distinct clipped vectors), and to the n^alpha regime with alpha > 1 needed for the transfer. Not closed by this step.
proved_step: THEOREM (subclass SPLIT(b)). Let n >= 8, b >= 0 fixed, W integer m x n, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1) log2 n). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * 2^(3n/4+1). PROOF. Let k = floor(n/2), s = n-k, x = (p,q) with p in {0,1}^k, q in {0,1}^s, and split W_j = (A_j, B_j). Let lo_j = sum_i min(0,B_ji) and hi_j = sum_i max(0,B_ji), so B_j.q lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j] for every q. Let tau_j(p) = t_j - A_j.p and clip_j(tau) = min(max(tau, lo_j), hi_j+1). Step 1: for every integer tau and every q, [B_j.q >= tau] = [B_j.q >= clip_j(tau)]. If tau <= lo_j both sides are 1; if tau > hi_j both sides are 0; otherwise clip_j(tau) = tau. Step 2: put kappa(p) = (clip_j(tau_j(p)))_j. Then f(p,q) = F(kappa(p), q), where F(K,q) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.q >= K_j] >= T]. Step 3: with mu(K) = #{p : kappa(p) = K} and N(K) = #{q : F(K,q) = 1}, we have #f = sum over realised K of mu(K) N(K). Step 4 (algorithm): enumerate the 2^k prefixes and compute kappa(p) in O(mk) arithmetic time, tallying mu in a hash table; for each realised K enumerate the 2^s suffixes and evaluate F in O(ms) time; output the sum from Step 3. Correctness follows from Steps 1-3. Step 5 (time): the first phase costs O(2^k m k). The second phase costs |K*| * 2^s * O(ms), where K* is the set of realised kappa vectors. Each K_j lies in {lo_j, ..., hi_j+1}, a set of size hi_j - lo_j + 2 = sum_i |B_ji| + 2 <= s n^b + 2 <= n^(b+1) (using n >= 8). So |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) = 2^(m(b+1)log2 n) <= 2^(n/4) by the bound on m. Hence the total time is poly(n,m) (2^(n/2) + 2^(n/4) 2^(n/2+1)) = poly(n,m) 2^(3n/4+1). QED. SCOPE. Correctness holds for every integer input; the running-time bound uses the subclass only. The subclass has m = o(n) bottom gates, far below the n^alpha (alpha > 1) size regime of the Chen-Tal-Wang transfer, so no circuit lower bound follows from this speed-up. OBSTACLE for linear m: the bound |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) needs m log n <= n/4; for m = Theta(n) the product of window sizes exceeds 2^(n/2). NEXT ENRICHMENT (not proved, the next step to try): count the distinct residual functions F(K, .) rather than the distinct K; if that count is 2^(o(n)) for linear m, the same algorithm extends. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session. Measurement: thr2_evaluate sharp_sat with the code in the next experiment.

proved_step: WINDOW LEMMA (exact-window interval class C(n,k,D)). Input: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=B, v_j in [-V,V], thresholds t_j, T. Class: there is an unknown column order pi* such that for each row j the nonzero columns of W_j are EXACTLY a block of k consecutive positions of pi*, and at most D rows share the same block. Claims: (a) Every ordering sigma under which every row's support is consecutive (C1P) satisfies nu(sigma) <= Dk, where nu(sigma) = max_p #{j : p in span_sigma(j)}. Proof: span = support = an interval of length k; the intervals of length k containing p are exactly k (left end in [p-k+1,p]); each exact interval has at most D rows. (b) A C1P ordering is found in time linear in the matrix size by a PQ-tree (Booth-Lueker); pi* is one such ordering. (c) For any ordering sigma, the DP over positions computes #{x: sum_j v_j [W_j.x>=t_j] >= T} exactly (induction on p: a gate is decided at its last support position; state = (sum of v over decided gates, partial sums of open gates)). (d) An open gate's partial sum lies in [-Bk,Bk], so the number of states at p is <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{nu(sigma)} <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{Dk}. With m <= Dn and k <= c n/(D log2 n), c<1: Dk log2(2Bk+1) = (c+o(1)) n, so the count is computed in time poly(n) 2^{(c+o(1)) n} on C(n,k,D). This is a speed-up over 2^n for windows of length Theta(n/log n). Gaps: (i) exact windows only (zero entries inside a window are excluded); (ii) the multiplicity D is essential, since without it nu can be m; (iii) (c) and (d) need an independent review; (e) the claim is not a speed-up for general THR o THR.

refuted_approach: G0007 decay form: 'Pr over a random restriction to p n free variables that a bottom gate is non-constant is at most exp(-c|S_j|)'. Reason: with small thresholds and dense supports, a gate is decided only if the free part is tiny, so the decay form cannot hold. lemma: Bounded-support reduction for THR o THR #SAT, exact for all integer weights. Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T], supp(j) = {i : W_ji != 0}, V2 = union of supp(j) over gates with |supp(j)| >= 2, V1 = (union of supp(j) over unary gates) minus V2, V0 = [n] minus (V1 union V2). proved_step: PROOF. Every gate is either supported in V2 (all gates with |supp| >= 2, and unary gates on V2) or a unary gate on a variable of V1; no unary gate sits on V0. A unary gate on i equals b0 + (b1 - b0) x_i with b1 - b0 in {-1,0,1}, so the top sum equals S(y) + c + sum_i a_i z_i, where y is the V2 part and z the V1 part of x. The indicator of f therefore depends only on (y,z), and the V0 bits are free, which gives the displayed formula. Algorithm: precompute once the sorted subset-sum lists of the two halves of V1 (2^{|V1|/2} entries each, O(2^{|V1|/2} poly) time). For each y (2^{|V2|} values), compute S(y) in poly(n,m) time and count pairs (l, r) with l + r >= theta(y) by a two-pointer pass over the sorted lists in O(2^{|V1|/2}) time. Total time poly(n,m) * 2^{|V2| + |V1|/2} = poly(n,m) * 2^{n - |V0| - |V1|/2}. Correctness holds for all integer weights because the formula is exact. proved_step: Bandwidth DP for THR o THR #SAT. Setting: variables 1..n in a FIXED order that is part of the input. Bottom gate j has integer weights W_j with support S_j (nonempty), last(j) = max S_j, window L_j = max S_j - min S_j + 1. Top gate: integer v_j, integer T, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let l = max_j L_j and V = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #f = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time O(n^2 m 2^(l-1) (2V+1)). Proof: process i = 1..n. Frontier F_i = {u <= i : u in S_j for some j with last(j) > i}. Claim |F_i| <= l-1. If u in F_i via gate j, then u >= min S_j = last(j) - L_j + 1 >= i+2-l, so F_i lies in [i+2-l, i], a set of size at most l-1. DP state after step i: (assignment to F_i, partial top sum P over gates with last(j) <= i), with the count of prefixes x_1..x_i producing it. Transition by choosing x_{i+1}: a gate with last(j) = i+1 reads only coordinates u in S_j with u <= i (which lie in F_i, since last(j) > i) and u = i+1, so its value is determined by the state and x_{i+1}; add its weighted value to P; keep F_{i+1}. Final answer = sum of counts over states with P >= T. Number of states at most 2^(l-1) (2V+1), since P lies in [-V, V]. Correctness follows by induction on i.

Algorithm: (a) for each unary gate on i in V1 set a_i += v_j (b1_j - b0_j), c += v_j b0_j, where b0_j = [0 >= t_j], b1_j = [W_ji >= t_j]; (b) let A be the remaining gates; for each y in {0,1}^{V2} compute S(y) = sum over A of v_j [W_j.y >= t_j] (A-gates have support inside V2, see the identity); (c) compute the distribution of sum_i a_i z_i over z in {0,1}^{V1} by an integer DP of range at most 4nmB+1; (d) output 2^{|V0|} * sum_y #{z : sum a_i z_i >= T - c - S(y)}. Correctness: the identity of S0007 (SURVIVED_REVIEW). Time: O(2^l (mn + n^2 m B)) arithmetic operations plus O(nmB) precomputation. lemma: LEMMA IW (windowed interval DP, exact for all integer weights). Setting: integers k>=1, D>=1, B>=0, n>=k. Bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{i=0}^{k-1} w_{j,i} x_{a_j+i} >= t_j] with 0 <= a_j <= n-k, |w_{j,i}| <= B, at most D gates per start a. Top f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], S = sum_j |v_j|. Then |f^{-1}(1)| is computed by a left-to-right DP over positions p = 0..n-1. State after reading x_0..x_{p-1}: key (c, (tau_j)_{j in A_p}), where c is the sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, A_p = gates with p-k+1 <= a_j <= p-1, and tau_j = clamp(t_j minus the read part of gate j, L_j, U_j+1), with [L_j,U_j] the range of the unread part of gate j's sum. Proof: (1) clamping preserves gate values; (2) the future depends only on the key, so equal keys can be merged; (3) U_j-L_j <= 2Bk, so tau_j takes <= 2Bk+2 values; c lies in an interval of S+1 integers; |A_p| <= D(k-1); so each level has <= (S+1)(2Bk+2)^{D(k-1)} keys; (4) each key has 2 transitions with O(Dk) updates, total O(n Dk^2 (S+1)(2Bk+2)^{D(k-1)}) integer operations. Scope: D = O(1) gives m = O(n) bottom gates, and k = n/log^2 n gives 2^{O(n/log n)} poly(n) time. This does NOT reach m = n^alpha (alpha>1), where D ~ n^{alpha-1} makes (2Bk+2)^{Dk} exceed 2^{o(n)}. proved_step: LEMMA-RO (random-order frontier DP, Las Vegas). Setting: fixed integers c,k >= 1; D = c(k-1); THR o THR circuit f = [sum_j v_j g_j >= T] with bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j], |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most c supports S_j, |v_j|, |w_{ji}| at most V(n) polynomial, any number m of gates. Let beta_D = (D/(D+1)) (D+1)^{-1/D} < 1. Claim: for every eps > 0 there is a Las Vegas algorithm computing #f exactly with expected time poly(n,m,V) 2^{(beta_D+eps) n}. Proof: (1) Fix an ordering pi of variables, pos(i) its position. Gate j completes at ct_j = max pos over S_j. K_t = {i : pos(i) <= t and some gate containing i completes after t}. A DP over x restricted to K_t plus the partial sum (range at most 2mV+1 values) is exact, because variables outside K_t are no longer read by any unfinished gate. State count at most 2^{|K_t|}(2mV+1). (2) i is in K_t iff pos(i) <= t and some u in N(i) has pos(u) > t, where N(i) is the union of S_j minus i over gates containing i; |N(i)| <= D. With s = |N(i)|+1 <= D+1 and tau = t/n: P(i in K_t) = P(pos(i) <= t) - P(all of {i} union N(i) in the prefix) <= tau - C(t,s)/C(n,s) <= tau - tau^{D+1} + O(D^2/n). Maximising over tau gives E|K_t| <= beta_D n + O(D^2). (3) A transposition of two positions changes the membership of at most 2(D+1) variables, so |K_t| is 2(D+1)-Lipschitz for transpositions. A Maurey/McDiarmid-type bound for uniform permutations gives deviation eps n with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(eps^2 n / D^2)); a union bound over t <= n gives, for large n, max_t |K_t| <= (beta_D+eps) n + O(D^2) with probability at least 1/2. (4) Algorithm: sample pi, compute max_t |K_t| exactly (poly time), accept if below the threshold, otherwise resample. Expected at most 2 trials; then run the DP. The output is exact; only the running time is random. Consequence: for fixed c,k, the subclass admits a counting algorithm with running time 2^{(beta_D+eps) n} poly(n,m,V), which is a strict 2^{(1-delta)n} saving with delta = 1 - beta_D - eps > 0 for any number of gates m, including m = n^alpha. The non-literal part has at most cn/2 gates by LEMMA-OVL.

lemma: Let W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, and let G(x) = ([w_j . x >= t_j])_j for x in {0,1}^n. Then the number of distinct rows of the 2^n x m matrix G is at most min(2^m, sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i)). Proof: (a) 2^m is trivial. (b) Replace t_j by t_j - 1/2. Since w_j . x - t_j is an integer, [w_j . x >= t_j] = [w_j . x > t_j - 1/2], so every cube point lies strictly off each shifted hyperplane. Each row is therefore the sign vector of a region of the arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^n, and such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions (Buck / Zaslavsky). Scope: integer data, any m, n. This is a bound on patterns only.
gap: Does NOT close G0001 or G0002: it bounds the pattern count, not the cost of enumerating realised patterns. Realised patterns cannot be enumerated from the region bound, because deciding whether a region contains a 0/1 point is hard extraction. For m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) >= 2^n, so it gives no saving.

proved_step: S0040 (CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: f(x) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [<w_{idx(j)}, x> >= t_j] >= T} for m bottom gates whose weight vectors take at most d distinct values w^(1..d) in Z^n with |w^(k)_i| <= B; t_j, v_j, T arbitrary integers. Claim: f is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^d (m d + 1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: DP over prefixes. For level i let z_k = <w^(k)_{<=i}, x_{<=i}> for k = 1..d; the state is z in Z^d. Since |z_k| <= B i <= Bn, there are at most (2Bn+1)^d states per level. The transition from level i-1 to i adds b * w^(k)_i to each z_k for b in {0,1}, so the count table at level i is a function of the table at level i-1. Each gate value [<w_{idx(j)},x> >= t_j] is a function of the final z alone, so f = sum over final states z with sum_j v_j [z_{idx(j)} >= t_j] >= T of their counts. Correctness is by induction on i. Scope: polynomial time when d is constant and B is polynomial in n. GAP: this does not close G0001. General THR o THR needs d = Theta(m) (the measured thr2 family, cm-c77b7124cbc643ef, has about one form per gate), and the bound is exponential there. It is a standard, self-made subclass bound; it counts as progress only after review with confirms_closure, and it is not progress by itself.
